name: Text Encryptor / Decryptor
description: Encrypt or decrypt text with a passphrase using real AES-256-GCM encryption and PBKDF2 key derivation, entirely in your browser — nothing is sent or stored.

faq.question: Is this real encryption, or just obfuscation?
faq.answer: Real encryption — AES-256-GCM (an authenticated cipher used throughout TLS and modern security software) with a key derived from your passphrase via PBKDF2 at 250,000 iterations, using your browser's native Web Crypto API. It's not a toy substitution cipher or base64 dressed up to look like encryption.

faq.question: What happens if I forget my passphrase?
faq.answer: The encrypted text becomes permanently unrecoverable — there is no backdoor, recovery key, or "forgot password" flow, by design. That's an inherent property of real encryption, not a limitation specific to this tool.

faq.question: Why does decryption sometimes fail even though I'm sure the passphrase is right?
faq.answer: AES-GCM is authenticated, meaning it verifies the ciphertext hasn't been altered as part of decrypting it — so a wrong passphrase and corrupted/tampered ciphertext both fail the same way, with no way to distinguish the two. Double-check for accidental whitespace or a truncated paste in the encrypted text field.
